key_insight: RAD-2 unifies a diffusion-based trajectory generator with a discriminator trained via reinforcement learning to provide corrective negative feedback, stabilizing multimodal closed-loop motion planning.
problem_solved: Diffusion planners model rich multimodal futures but suffer stochastic instabilities and lack corrective feedback when trained only by imitation, yielding poor closed-loop robustness for high-level autonomous driving.
method: Generator: diffusion-based sampler produces multimodal trajectory hypotheses capturing future uncertainty.
Discriminator/Critic: learned evaluator provides negative feedback (penalizes unsafe/unrealistic behaviors) and trains with RL/adversarial objectives.
Unified training loop: hybrid imitation + RL losses with closed-loop rollouts to scale stability and corrective learning.
impact: Provides a scalable way to stabilize generative trajectory planners for robust closed-loop control, improving safety and reliability in autonomous driving and other sequential decision tasks.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing generator (diffusion) → trajectories → discriminator (critic) → corrective signal loop back into generator
Before vs after chart of closed-loop stability / failure rate comparing pure imitation vs RAD-2
Multimodal trajectory plot: sampled futures with uncertainty cones and discriminator-highlighted corrections
Training flowchart: imitation loss + RL/adversarial loss + closed-loop environment rollouts
paper_title: RAD-2: Scaling Reinforcement Learning in a Generator-Discriminator Framework
paper_authors: Hao Gao, Shaoyu Chen, Yifan Zhu, Yuehao Song, Wenyu Liu
